title: Augmented Computational Design
venue: Artificial Intelligence in Performance-Driven Design: Theories, Methods, and Tools Towards Sustainability
extended_summary:
This chapter addresses how artificial intelligence can be used in generative design, with a focus on performance-driven architectural and engineering design. The central problem is that design decisions are often numerous, discrete, and interdependent, while desired outcomes are few and high-level; the authors argue that this makes conventional direct reasoning about design space exploration difficult. They propose an “Augmented Computational Design” framework that formalizes design as a pairing of decision space and performance space and distinguishes two dual tasks: mapping many design choices to a small number of outcomes, and navigating backward from desired outcomes to valid design choices.

The proposed approach is largely theoretical and mathematical. It draws on multi-variate calculus, Jacobian approximation, singular value decomposition, and pseudo-inverse reasoning to describe how data-driven models can support both evaluation and derivation in design. The paper also situates several AI methods along a spectrum of generative design approaches, focusing on statistical AI methods such as probabilistic graphical models, Bayesian Belief Networks, and diffusion-like ideas, while contrasting them with rule-based, optimization-based, and model-driven methods.

To illustrate the framework, the chapter presents a case study from Dutch building energy modelling (NTA 8800). In that example, a surrogate Bayesian Belief Network is trained to approximate an opaque government energy-performance calculation tool using sampled simulations, sensitivity analysis, and discretization of inputs. The illustrative context is architectural and policy-oriented rather than educational, and the chapter concludes that the framework can improve explainability and make complex design-performance relationships more tractable, especially when only a few important outputs must be linked to many design variables.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a conceptual/book-chapter style methodological treatise with an illustrative case study, not a controlled empirical evaluation. The excerpt reports a workflow and claims of feasibility, but no rigorous causal design, no peer-reviewable effect estimates for learner outcomes, and no validated educational experiment.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper suggests practical value for improving the efficiency and interpretability of complex building-energy decision support, but the impact is indirect and not quantified with effect sizes. It is relevant to institutional decision-making, yet the demonstrated gains are methodological rather than measured outcomes.

interventions.use_case: Probabilistic meta-modelling and Bayesian Belief Network (BBN) surrogate modeling for architectural/building energy performance analysis, used to approximate a Dutch government NTA 8800 calculation model from sampled input parameters and sensitivity-selected variables.

finding.finding_summary: The chapter argues that an AI-based surrogate model can make building energy performance assessment faster and more tractable than the original NTA 8800 Excel tool, which only handles one scenario at a time and is not traceable to inputs. The demonstration uses 20,000 Sobol-sampled simulations and then reduces 269 inputs to 15 influential parameters, with those 15 explaining about 90.45% to 92.30% of the final energy performance score; however, no formal effect size or validation metric values are reported in the excerpt.
finding.measure: Computational feasibility, sensitivity-reduced input dimensionality, and surrogate-model approximation quality (NRMSE, MAPE mentioned but values not reported)

finding.finding_summary: The chapter presents the AI surrogate as useful for policy analysis and building-energy governance, especially for advising on subsidy policy, building-code compliance, and energy transition planning in the Netherlands. It frames the BBN meta-model as a way to support institutional decision-making by translating a complex regulatory calculation tool into a more usable, interpretable approximation, but it does not report experimental policy effects.
finding.measure: Policy-analysis utility and governance applicability of the surrogate model
